scope.summary: Implement the channel registry core per Section 13.17 (BK-17.1, TAI-BK-031/032), closing REQ-043: the canonical BodyChannel type (channel_id BCH-, stable snake_case channel_key, kind Skeletal|Tissue, group_key, region_mask_ref, ChannelRange {min, max, design_max}, default) with registration enforcement — a channel must exist as a bodykit_channel_registry row before any morph asset referencing it may be imported, and unregistered channels are not evaluable.
acceptance_criteria: BodyChannel, ChannelKind (Skeletal|Tissue, snake_case serde), and ChannelRange {min, max, design_max} exist exactly as specified in TAI-BK-031 with Serialize/Deserialize/JsonSchema derives.
register_channel persists a BCH- row via guarded storage and rejects duplicate channel_key, non-snake_case keys, and ranges violating min <= default <= max <= design_max.
Importing a morph asset whose channel_key is not registered fails with a typed error (registration-before-import enforcement, TAI-BK-032).
The solver-side evaluator refuses to evaluate a channel key absent from the loaded registry snapshot (typed error, not silent zero).
channel_key lookups are exposed for API/MCP surfaces: list_channels(group_key) and get_channel(channel_key) return typed rows.
scope.risk_if_missed: Without a typed registry with registration-before-import, channels become ad-hoc strings scattered across assets — unaddressable for LLM workflows (REQ-043) and unenforceable for the decoupling law, which is BodyKit's founding requirement.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > BodyKit shape channels and measurements

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT owns authoritative, job, or external-tool lifecycle events and must project the same event_id, run_id, actor_id, and correlation_id from EventLedger into Flight Recorder.
This MT must wire the shared internal_diagnostics API for its native, job, device, solver-run, or DCC failure modes with bounded structured evidence.
The owning native shell or scheduled job supplies Palmistry coverage; this MT must preserve operation identity and recovery handles.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

required_changes_before_execution: Separate control independence from declared feathered deformation support, skeletal propagation, physical response, and explicit coupling.
Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.

requirements: Resolve Principal, AuthenticatedSession and AccessSpace before every resource read or mutation.

Use authenticated SurrealDB record-user table/field PERMISSIONS intersected with ResourceBroker-backed artifact/file handles; administrative/root credentials and UI filtering are never the security boundary. PostgreSQL and SQLite access paths are forbidden.
Derived resources preserve the intersection of source access scopes and must not leak existence through counts, search, previews, logs, traces, caches, diagnostics, exports or model context.
